I loved their style of government, and the fact that citizenship wasn't guaranteed. The lecture scene when the main character was in high school is classic, and should be read by everyone.

Citizenship wasn't guaranteed but it was open to absolutely everyone and the only thing you needed to do was to not quit or die before your contract of service was up. (Of course, the war does extend the contracts, but that makes sense.)

It was one of my favorite books when I was an adolescent and I have reread it several times over the last 40 years or so.

I really like the discussions in history and moral philosophy. I also really like the concept of the MI suits.

Heinlein was a graduate of the Naval Academy and I suspect he spent some time around Marines because his descriptions of the MI and the Navy in his future sound a lot like a description of the USMC and USN.
